method: BASELINE. Written straight from the deposited text with the writing-l4-rules skill (and references/regulative.md), from the seat of the individual to whom the law is applied, with the design defaults ruled on 2026-10-18 and the rulings on negatives of 2026-11-04 and 2026-11-05 (JUST FALSE where the text says no, NOTHING with a NOTHING-kind tag where it does not answer); the rules in one module, the dates in another, the questions in one seat module importing them; three regulative rules (ss 71(2), 87(3)(c), 89(3)) run by EVALTRACE inside exported questions that take only plain facts; no REFUSE; checked with the stable l4 of VS Code extension 1.6.98, JL4_LIBRARY_PATH unset. No pipeline, no coverage table, no independent test pass, no human gate.

seat: the person with a claim in a representative proceeding (class action) in the Supreme Court of Tasmania: the individual who brings it (the representative party) or a group member or sub-group member on whose behalf it is brought (rp-seat.l4)

checks.command: l4 run rp-dates.l4 ; l4 run rp-rules.l4 ; l4 run rp-seat.l4 ; l4 run rp-cases.l4
checks.result: 157 assertions written, 157 satisfied, 0 errors, 0 warnings in every file (2026-11-07)
checks.note: l4 run exits 0 even when an assertion fails, so the diagnostics are what was read. Expected values worked by hand from the text.
